strongest_angle: The Hubble Space Telescope successfully detected the secondary eclipse of the ultra-short-period rocky exoplanet TOI-2431b for the first time, providing a dayside brightness temperature of 2524 K and combining near-infrared observations with TESS optical data.

key_facts.fact: The Hubble Space Telescope detected the secondary eclipse of the rocky exoplanet TOI-2431b for the first time in the near infrared using its Wide Field Camera 3.
The secondary eclipse points to a dayside brightness temperature of 2524 K for the rocky planet TOI-2431b.
The Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) spotted the ultra-short-period rocky planet TOI-2431b in the year 2019 with an orbital period of 5.4 hours.
The Leiden Observatory presented an HST/WFC3 G141 phase-curve observation of TOI-2431b combining Hubble and TESS optical eclipse measurements.
